q: Define rights (Hodder).
a: Basic claims and entitlements human beings have simply because they are human, allowing them to live safe, meaningful and dignified lives.

q: Define justice (Hodder).
a: An ethical concept about how people should or should not be treated; usually being treated fairly and getting what one deserves.

q: When was the UDHR adopted and what was the vote?
a: 10 December 1948, UNGA Resolution 217 A (III): 48 in favour, 0 against, 8 abstentions.

q: Which states abstained on the UDHR in 1948?
a: The six Soviet-bloc states (USSR, Byelorussian SSR, Ukrainian SSR, Poland, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia), plus Saudi Arabia and South Africa.

q: Name the Chair, Vice-Chair and Rapporteur of the first UN Commission on Human Rights.
a: Eleanor Roosevelt (USA) Chair, Peng-chun Chang (China) Vice-Chair, Charles Malik (Lebanon) Rapporteur.

q: Distinguish negative and positive rights.
a: Negative rights require those with power to refrain from acting (e.g. UDHR Art. 5, no torture). Positive rights require authorities to take action (e.g. UDHR Art. 26, education). In practice they overlap, as Hodder's prison example shows.

q: What are Karel Vasak's three generations of rights?
a: 1st generation, liberty: civil and political rights. 2nd, equality: economic, social and cultural rights. 3rd, fraternity: collective or solidarity rights such as development and a clean environment. Based on the French Revolution slogan.

q: Give the classic example of a collective right.
a: Self-determination: a people's right to choose its own government and form a state if it wishes (e.g. Palestinians, Catalans).

q: Define cultural relativism.
a: The view that each culture has its own moral code, so right and wrong should be set locally rather than by a universal authority like the UN; it sees UDHR universality as imposing Western values.

q: How many executions did Amnesty record in 2025, and how many in 2024?
a: At least 2,707 in 17 countries in 2025 (excluding China's thousands), up 78% from 1,518 in 2024. Iran carried out 2,159 or more.

q: Which Indian constitutional article and Act make education a positive right, and when did the Act come into force?
a: Article 21A (86th Amendment, 2002); the RTE Act 2009, in force from 1 April 2010. It requires schools to reserve 25% of seats for disadvantaged children, a quota the Supreme Court upheld on 12 April 2012.

q: What did Pramati Educational & Cultural Trust (6 May 2014) decide?
a: A five-judge Supreme Court bench held that the RTE Act does not apply to minority schools, whether aided or unaided, protecting the collective rights of minorities under Art. 30. It was referred for reconsideration in September 2025.

q: What is Article 44 of the Indian Constitution, and which state first implemented a UCC?
a: Article 44 is a Directive Principle that the State shall endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code. Uttarakhand implemented one on 27 January 2025.

q: What did Navtej Singh Johar v Union of India (6 Sept 2018) decide?
a: A five-judge bench unanimously struck down Section 377 IPC as far as it criminalised consensual adult same-sex relations, overruling Koushal (2013). Section 377 was a colonial-era law.

q: What did Shayara Bano v Union of India (22 Aug 2017) decide?
a: By a 3:2 majority, the Supreme Court held instant triple talaq unconstitutional.

q: State Rawls's key ideas on egalitarian justice.
a: A Theory of Justice (1971): justice as fairness, choosing principles behind a veil of ignorance to benefit the least advantaged. Each person has an inviolability that even the welfare of society as a whole cannot override.

q: What conditions does cosmopolitan justice set for humanitarian intervention?
a: The state is structurally unjust (abusive or failed), the intervention will succeed, and it is a last resort.

q: Which country hosted the most refugees at mid-2022, and what share of refugees do low- and middle-income countries host (UNHCR, end-2025)?
a: Türkiye, with 3,673,808 refugees (Hodder/UNHCR). At end-2025, low- and middle-income countries hosted 68% and neighbouring countries 65%.

q: What is ecological justice, and which constitution first gave nature rights?
a: Justice for all living beings, which have moral considerability. Ecuador's 2008 Constitution, Art. 71, gave rights to Pacha Mama (Nature).

q: What is Ubuntu, and give the TRC amnesty figures.
a: A Zulu philosophy of community-centred, restorative justice ('my humanity is inextricably bound up in yours', Tutu). The TRC received 7,112 amnesty applications: 849 granted, 5,392 refused.
